The Independent Directors of Irish Continental Group, plc (“ICG”) are pleased to announce that the scheme of arrangement under Chapter 1 of Part 9 of the Companies Act 2014 (the “Scheme”) in connection with the final recommended cash offer by Bluefin Bidco Limited (“BidCo”), for the entire issued and to be issued share capital of ICG (other than the Excluded Shares) (the “Acquisition”), became effective today 20 November 2026 (the “Effective Date”).

In accordance with the requirements of the Irish Takeover Rules, all consideration paid by BidCo to Scheme Shareholders under the terms of the Scheme will be distributed by no later than 4 December 2026.

Cancellation of the admission of ICG Units to trading on the regulated market of Euronext Dublin and the listing of ICG Units on the Official List of Euronext Dublin is expected to occur at 7.00 a.m. on 23 November 2026 (being the first business day following the Effective Date). Cancellation of the admission of ICG Units to trading on the Main Market of the London Stock Exchange and the FCA’s Official List is expected to occur at 8.00 a.m on 23 November 2026 (being the first business day following the Effective Date).

Capitalised terms used, but not defined, in this Announcement have the same meaning as in the Scheme Document dated 5 August 2026. All times stated in this Announcement are to time in Dublin.

data.title: Sky Protocol sees $2 billion in stablecoin withdrawals, disputes illicit fund claims
data.description:
Sky Protocol processed more than $2 billion in stablecoin redemptions on Thursday, the same day a CoinDesk investigation linked $518 million in transactions through the protocol to illicit activity.

The withdrawals involved users exchanging Sky’s USDS stablecoin for Circle’s USDC through its Peg Stability Module (PSM), a system that allows users to swap the tokens at a fixed rate.

Sky, which has a total value locked (TVL) of $2.3 billion, said on Friday in a statement that USDS maintained its $1 peg throughout the withdrawals. According to the protocol, the amount of USDC held in the PSM never fell below $800 million and had climbed back above $1.1 billion by Friday.

Sky also challenged the investigation, pointing to a review by Block Analitica, which notably serves as a risk adviser to the Sky ecosystem.

The withdrawals came amid concerns raised by the investigation that Circle could freeze USDC held by Sky, potentially making it harder for users to redeem their stablecoins.

Related: Circle freezes $12.6M of USDC linked to privacy protocol Zama

Sky disputes findings on illicit transactions

CoinDesk’s Nov. 19 report looked at research by blockchain analytics firm Inca Digital, which identified $518 million in transactions involving wallets linked to hackers, sanctioned entities, and other threat actors over a span of five years.

Of that amount, around $101.9 million was linked to North Korean actors, including wallets connected to the February 2025 Bybit hack.

Meanwhile, Block Analitica disputed some parts of the investigation, saying that the $518 million represented less than 0.06% of the more than $960 billion processed through Sky’s peg stability modules.

The firm said about two-thirds of the flagged activity occurred between 2021 and mid-2024 – before Sky introduced its newer LitePSM system.

Block Analitica also questioned the reported links to North Korean threat actors, stating that some wallets were several transactions removed from known addresses and may have belonged to unrelated users.

The firm added that most of the flagged transactions passed through trading services such as 1inch, ParaSwap and MetaMask Swaps, which automatically choose where to route trades.

Sky says reserves remain strong despite withdrawals

The large withdrawals also came amid a sharp drop in the number of USDS tokens in circulation. The supply fell nearly 40% in one day to about 3.2 billion tokens, according to DefiLlama data. However, the stablecoin maintained its $1 value despite the decline.

CoinDesk reported that a wallet linked to crypto exchange Poloniex accounted for a large share of the withdrawals, although it wasn’t clear whether the exchange itself was behind the transactions.

The combined circulating supply of Sky’s USDS and DAI stablecoins fell to $6.11 billion as of Nov. 20, down 37.8% over the past 30 days. Source: Sky Ecosystem Financial Insights

Sky said it held about $9.3 billion in assets backing its stablecoins as of Friday, compared with around $6.11 billion in USDS and DAI in circulation, according to its financial dashboard. The dashboard also showed about $93 million in reserves to help cover potential losses.

Cointelegraph reached out to the Sky Frontier Foundation for comment but had not received a response by publication.

data.title: European emissions proposal faces Middle East pushback at UN aviation agency
data.description:
By Allison Lampert

Plans to change the European Union's Emissions Trading System faced pushback at a global aviation gathering that wraps up on Friday, as Middle East countries challenged fresh efforts to curb pollution from airlines outside an existing deal.

It is the latest revolt within the aviation sector over plans to expand Europe's biggest climate change policy to cover flights to third-country destinations within 5,000 km (3,107 miles) of Frankfurt Airport, starting in 2029. The ETS currently applies to flights within the European Economic Area.

Saudi Arabia urged International Civil Aviation Organization member countries to support a global approach to countering emissions under the decade-old Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation. Saudi Arabia wants CORSIA, an ICAO program that is mandatory for most airlines, to be the only emissions plan covering international aviation.

Qatar also proposed that ICAO undertake a technical assessment of the implications of the EU ETS for CORSIA.

Several European countries disagreed with the two Middle East countries' positions.

Under CORSIA, airlines in most countries have to buy offsets in environmental projects to counter their rising emissions from international flights.

The airline industry has pledged to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050, but executives acknowledge the target will be difficult to hit due to shortages of green jet fuel and increasing passenger traffic.

Airlines and most countries support CORSIA to avoid a patchwork of emissions programs that they argue would raise costs. But some European lawmakers and environmental groups have argued CORSIA does not go far enough to reduce international aviation emissions.

Under the EU proposal, the 5,000-km distance would cover flights to airports in the Middle East and North Africa but omit transatlantic flights to the United States.

Saudi Arabia, supported by Kuwait, Qatar and Egypt, urged countries and regional organizations to avoid overlapping and double charging under "duplicative or extraterritorial emissions trade schemes that will increase compliance costs, create administrative burdens and distort competition."

ICAO cannot impose rules on its 193 member states, but its decisions influence national regulations.

data.title: China's BYD has SUV that infringes on JLR Defender design, Dutch court rules
data.description:
By Nick Carey

A judge at the Dutch district court in The Hague ruled on Friday that a large SUV made by BYD infringes on the design of Jaguar Land Rover's popular Defender model and imposed a temporary injunction prohibiting the Chinese automaker from selling the vehicle in the European Union.

JLR, a unit of India's Tata Motors , launched the case earlier this year after BYD announced on its UK web site that the seven-seater Ti7 SUV was available for orders with deliveries to customers starting in January 2027.

BYD launched the Fangchengbao Ti7 in China last year.

"In these summary proceedings, the preliminary relief judge rules that the Ti7 infringes the EU design of Jaguar Land Rover," the court ruling said. "The characteristic and distinctive elements of the design are reflected in the BYD Ti7."

The temporary injunction is for a week because the court found that BYD "currently has no concrete plans to place the Ti7 on the market in the EU."

The judge ruled, however, that the court had no jurisdiction over BYD's affiliate in the United Kingdom.

It is rare in Europe for major automakers to go to court over design rights infringement. It is also uncommon for such a ruling to come so early in proceedings of a case that is ongoing and likely to last for some time.

"We protect our intellectual property and take legal action when necessary," JLR said in a statement. "Legal proceedings are ongoing, and we won’t be commenting further at this time."

Legacy automakers have often complained that Chinese automakers have copied designs, though little has been proven in court. In 2005, for instance, General Motors and Chinese rival Chery settled a case over the Chery QQ that the No. 1 US automaker said was a copy of its Chevrolet Spark.

In a statement, BYD said it "strongly disagrees" with the ruling and will appeal it.

"The BYD Ti 7 is the result of BYD's own independent design work and infringes none of JLR's rights," BYD said. "We will pursue every legal avenue to demonstrate that this decision is incorrect."

BYD has grown rapidly in Europe since launching sales on the continent in late 2022. According to ACEA data, this year through September the Chinese automaker's sales more than doubled to over 280,000 vehicles in Europe versus the same period last year, outselling Ford, Tesla and Nissan.

data.title: The CEO Who Thinks Corporate America Failed the Political Test — WSJ
data.description:
By Chip Cutter

Patagonia has never worried too much about who it might bother with its corporate activism.

The outdoor-apparel maker has fought for causes from the environment to better voting access and — to the chagrin of finance bros everywhere — restricted its custom-branded vests to firms that "prioritize the planet" for a stretch. (It has since tweaked the policy.)

In September, it joined conservation groups in suing the Trump administration over plans to scale back protected national monuments in Utah.

Ryan Gellert, who became Patagonia's chief executive in 2020, said the company isn't inherently partisan — though it does have an agenda. "We're not an extension of the Democratic Party, and we're not in opposition to the concept of the Republican Party," he said. "We're in full alignment with anybody that wants to save our home planet."

Over the years, Patagonia has honed a playbook for how to speak out on topics it cares about and mostly sidestepped the blowback other brands have run into. (See Target or Bud Light.)

Gellert spoke with The Wall Street Journal about how companies navigate Washington and more. This interview has been edited for clarity.

You've watched as companies dialed back diversity efforts and retrenched on social issues. What's the lesson you see in how they've responded to pressures?

The companies getting it wrong are pretty consistently the companies that have tried to have it both ways. So the companies that say, "I don't know what's important to me. Wait a second, I've got to pretend this is important to me. Wait a second, it pissed somebody off; I've got to pretend it's not important to me." I mean, people sniff that out in seconds, and you're just in the crosshairs from all sides.

One company that does exceptional work on this, and it's rooted in consistency and clarity of values is Costco. Their position — I'm not sure they think of it as a big position — is: These are our values, and with all due respect, don't tell us how to run our f — ing business. We know how to do this, and so we will. I really, really, really respect that.

Well, some might say Patagonia is in a rare spot: You can advocate differently, given your brand.

Yeah, I think that's bulls — . I will say this: We have incredibly unique founders. We put together and pioneered a very unique ownership and stewardship model, and we've got this history.

What I get really frustrated by is a total lack of commitment: Even publicly traded companies find it very comforting to hide behind their structure, and therefore they can't do anything else. I just reject that out of hand.

My expectation is not that CEOs of every company speak out on every topic, but it sure as hell is that they understand the values of their organization, and they stand up and provide leadership when it's appropriate.

Patagonia used to be the unofficial uniform of Wall Street and Silicon Valley. At some point, you restricted corporate logos on some of your clothing.

We did. That took on a life of its own, so let me clarify the reality.

What's the state of things now?

That's a piece of business we still do. We took a pause for a minute, but this was primarily the problem we were trying to solve: We make product and engineer into it as much quality as we know how, and we want that product to exist as long as possible.

If you have a broken zipper, get it back to us and we'll fix it for you. If you have a product that is usable and you're done using it, get it back to us and we'll find somebody to use it.

We came to understand that if you embroidered a logo and the employees left the company, the product became virtually unusable. So the biggest problem we had to solve was how do we apply logos in a way that's not got that level of permanence?

We're thoughtful about both industries and customers and value alignment and who we sell to. You're not going to get me to go through a list of who we do and don't.

So if an AI company says, "We want to buy a ton of Patagonia stuff with our logo on it," how do you feel about that?

I'm quite certain if it did happen, I would be pulled into that conversation. How would I navigate that?

It would be unlikely that we would do it, candidly, but it's a hypothetical. The determinant would not be a commercial one.

I hate to frame it like this, but is climate change an opportunity for your business?

It's a funny dynamic being a company that makes technical products for outdoor sports, and then one whose mission statement is we're in business to save our home planet. Both can be true. The climate is driving different weather patterns, and in the business, you ask yourself: Do you create products that people want in this environment? The answer, of course, is yes. Rain protection is a key part of that. So is insect repellency. So is UPF and sun repellency.

How do you view AI's potential impact on jobs?

No. 1, we're continuing to hire people. No. 2, we have always had a bias, and that bias remains toward promoting internally where that's the best decision for the company.

We're talking today on Anthropic's IPO, and they've got a valuation that's historically high. What is it going to take for that to pay off? It's going to take tremendous efficiency, which is a nice way of saying reducing people and their cost from businesses. That really concerns me.

Does this change how you make employment decisions? We've seen the drip-drip-drip of layoff announcements across companies.

I've gone through one round of layoffs in my career that I was responsible for: It was a small percentage, about 35 roles. It didn't feel small to the 35 people who were impacted.

At Patagonia?

It was Patagonia. I don't want to hide from that. That was in reorganizing our business a couple of years ago. Not to a single person did that feel like a small thing. It felt like a failure of leadership when we went through that, and I think that it is.

One of the biggest things we've got to address at the intersection of business and government is the lack of trust in institutions. When CEOs say one thing and do another and are sort of cavalier or callous toward the impact of their decisions on employees, I don't think they deserve trust.

Write to Chip Cutter at chip.cutter@wsj.com

data.title: 53rd Consecutive Year of Dividend Increases for United Bankshares, Inc.
data.description:
United Bankshares, Inc. (“United”) () today announced that its Board of Directors declared a fourth quarter dividend of $0.38 per share for shareholders of record as of December 11, 2026. Dividends per share of $1.52 for the year 2026 represents an increase over the $1.49 per share paid for the year of 2025.

The dividend payout of approximately $51.1 million on 134.5 million shares is payable January 4, 2027. The year 2026 marks the 53rd consecutive year of dividend increases to United shareholders. United is one of only two major banking companies in the USA to have increased its dividend to shareholders for at least 53 consecutive years.

United Bankshares, Inc. is a financial services company with consolidated assets of approximately $34 billion as of September 30, 2026. It is the parent company of United Bank, which comprises over 240 offices located across Washington, D.C., Virginia, West Virginia, Maryland, North Carolina, South Carolina, Ohio, Pennsylvania, and Georgia. For more information, visit ubsi-inc.com.

data.title: AVCF Invests Rs 60 Cr In SatSure, Leads First Close Of Rs 200 Cr Series B Round
data.description:
The Antariksh Venture Capital Fund (AVCF), backed by the Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre (IN-SPACe) and managed by SIDBI Venture Capital Ltd (SVCL), has invested Rs 60 crore in Bengaluru-based Earth intelligence startup SatSure. The investment marks the first close of the company’s Rs 200 crore Series B funding round, as per a media report.

The transaction is AVCF’s first investment in the downstream data analytics and artificial intelligence (AI) segment of India’s space economy. It expands the fund’s investment focus beyond launch services and satellite hardware to commercial space-data infrastructure catering to enterprise and government customers.

Arup Kumar, managing director and chief executive officer of SIDBI Venture Capital, said the investment aligns with AVCF’s mandate to support the growth of India’s private space ecosystem and back companies combining indigenous space infrastructure with downstream commercial applications. He added that the fund would continue to deploy institutional capital in space-tech businesses targeting international markets.

How SatSure Plans To Use The Funding

The investment will support four key areas of SatSure’s operations, in line with India’s space commercialisation roadmap.

The company plans to advance its optical payloads ahead of a proposed orbital flight in 2027 and execute a multi-satellite constellation mandate under the IN-SPACe-anchored Earth Observation Public-Private Partnership (EO-PPP).

The funding will also help scale Dhaarini, SatSure’s Large Earth Observation Model. The platform had earlier received a grant of Rs 24.6 crore under IN-SPACe’s Technology Adoption Fund (TAF).

SatSure also plans to expand its international commercial operations from India.

The ongoing Series B round comprises Rs 165 crore in primary equity, Rs 25 crore in venture debt and Rs 10 crore through secondary transactions. The company expects to complete the round on a rolling basis by December 2026.

Following the first close, SatSure’s cumulative institutional capital raised has reached Rs 427 crore, excluding government grants.

SatSure’s Full-Stack Earth Intelligence Business

SatSure operates through two entities, covering satellite hardware and downstream data analytics.

Its subsidiary, KaleidEO, develops optical satellite payloads and builds complete satellites under India’s Earth Observation Public-Private Partnership for the national Earth observation constellation.

SatSure uses Earth observation data to provide decision intelligence to banks, insurers, critical infrastructure companies and government agencies. Its operations cover the value chain, from satellite payloads and geospatial foundation models to AI, analytics and industry-specific applications.

Prateep Basu, chief executive officer and co-founder of SatSure, said the company’s business model focuses on managing the entire Earth intelligence value chain, from collecting satellite data to converting it into actionable insights through AI and foundation models. He added that the Series B funding would support the expansion of these capabilities from India to international markets.

SatSure’s Banking And Financial Services Presence

SatSure’s technology is already integrated into India’s financial infrastructure. Its SatSource product line is part of the Reserve Bank of India’s Unified Lending Interface (ULI).

According to the company, public-sector banks, including State Bank of India, use its platform to assess farm loan applications in minutes, compared with processes that earlier took weeks.

The company has 24 banking and financial services customers. These include HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank, which are both investors in and customers of SatSure.

Its earlier funding rounds were backed by Baring Private Equity Partners India, Promus Ventures, Asian Development Bank Ventures, Omidyar Network India, now Prana Ventures, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Kotak Mahindra Bank and Nuvama Asset Management, among others.

India’s Space Economy And Startup Funding

India’s space economy is projected to grow from approximately USD 8.4 billion in 2023 to USD 40–45 billion by 2030, according to a Jefferies report. The government has set a target of developing a USD 100 billion space economy by 2040.

The number of registered space startups in India has increased from one in 2014 to around 440 as of August 2026, according to government data.

Nine startups identified by Jefferies have collectively raised approximately USD 539 million, while cumulative private investment in the broader space ecosystem reached nearly USD 600 million by FY26.

Among the prominent companies in the sector, Skyroot Aerospace has raised USD 160 million, Pixxel USD 95 million, Agnikul Cosmos USD 76 million and Digantara USD 65 million.

data.title: Sensex Jumps Nearly 900 Pts, Nifty Reclaims 25,800; Investors' Wealth Rises Rs 2.18 Lakh Cr
data.description:
Both the Sensex and Nifty gain more than 2.5 per cent during the week, marking their fourth consecutive weekly advance

Indian equities extended their rally for a second straight session on Friday, with the Nifty closing above 25,800 for the first time since 18 February. Strong buying in banking, information technology and realty stocks helped benchmarks overcome a weak opening and finish close to their session highs.

The Nifty recovered sharply from its early low of 25,345.20, eventually climbing to an intraday high of 25,808.80. The BSE Sensex advanced 897.96 points, or 1.08 per cent, to settle at 83,919.71, while the NSE Nifty 50 gained 286.30 points, or 1.12 per cent, to close at 25,800.60.

The rally also strengthened the weekly performance of domestic equities. Both the Sensex and Nifty gained more than 2.5 per cent during the week, marking their fourth consecutive weekly advance.

Investor wealth received a boost of more than Rs 2 lakh crore during Friday's session. The total market capitalisation of BSE-listed companies increased to Rs 514.15 lakh crore from Rs 511.97 lakh crore in the previous session, adding approximately Rs 2.18 lakh crore.

Banking Stocks Hit Record Highs, IT Joins Rally

Banking stocks were among the biggest contributors to Friday's gains. The Nifty Private Bank index rose 3 per cent to a fresh record high, while the Nifty Bank index also touched an all-time high after advancing 2.5 per cent. The Nifty Realty index gained 1.7 per cent, also reaching a record level.

The Nifty PSU Bank index climbed 1.2 per cent, moving closer to its previous record high. The IT index advanced 1.3 per cent, providing further support to the benchmarks.

The rally was not universal, however. The Nifty Media index declined nearly 2 per cent, making it the weakest sectoral performer. Metal and consumer durables stocks also ended lower, shedding between 0.2 per cent and 0.4 per cent.

The broader market lagged the frontline indices. The Nifty Midcap index gained 0.6 per cent, while the Nifty Smallcap index ended marginally lower.

Among Nifty constituents, Apollo Hospitals, Axis Bank, Max Healthcare, HDFC Bank and Maruti Suzuki were the leading gainers. Titan Company, Tata Steel, NTPC, Eternal and Hindustan Unilever (HUL) featured among the biggest losers.

Ashoka Buildcon, Urban Company Among Stock-Specific Movers

At the stock level, Ashoka Buildcon declined 2 per cent after its Rs 846.38 crore Saudi Arabian project was cancelled by Diriyah Company.

Urban Company fell 4 per cent after raising Rs 2,500 crore through a qualified institutional placement (QIP). Allied Blenders and Distillers slipped 2 per cent after filing an appeal before the Bombay High Court challenging an arbitrator's order.

On the gaining side, Firstsource Solutions advanced 3 per cent following its partnership with SEW.AI. Kirloskar Brothers also rose 3 per cent after securing orders worth Rs 366 crore.

data.title: Bharath Vasudevan Returns To Capital One To Lead India Technology Centre
data.description:
The former BCG partner returns to Capital One with over 25 years of experience across financial services, technology, analytics and risk management

Capital One Financial Corporation has appointed Bharath Vasudevan as Senior Vice President and Head of Capital One India, where he will lead the company's technology centre in Bengaluru and oversee its strategic direction, operations and innovation initiatives.

Vasudevan brings more than 25 years of global leadership experience across technology solutioning, risk management, analytics and financial services. His appointment marks his return to Capital One after a previous tenure of nearly a decade at Capital One Services.

In his new role, Vasudevan will oversee the organisation's work across artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, data science and modern software engineering. He will also focus on strengthening integration with global enterprise teams to develop technology solutions for the company's customers worldwide.

The appointment reflects Capital One's continued investment in India as a strategic centre for technology talent, innovation and global collaboration.

Leadership Experience Across Financial Services

Before returning to Capital One, Vasudevan held senior leadership positions across financial services and technology. Most recently, he served as a Partner at Boston Consulting Group (BCG), working at the intersection of financial services, technological innovation, risk management and enterprise-wide digital transformation.

He has also served as Chief Revenue Officer at deep-tech firm Trusting Social and held an executive leadership position in the Enterprise Risk Office at Bajaj Finserv. His professional experience spans technology-led business transformation, advanced analytics and risk management.

Welcoming Vasudevan, Girish Bachani, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer, Capital One Financial Services, said India plays a critical role in the company's global technology ecosystem, supporting its foundational platforms, AI capabilities and data-driven solutions.

Bachani added that Vasudevan's experience in advanced analytics, risk management and large-scale transformation, along with his familiarity with Capital One's culture, would support the expansion of the India centre's capabilities and its contribution to global operations.

Commenting on his appointment, Vasudevan said he looked forward to leading the India centre and working on products that address complex challenges in financial services. He highlighted Capital One's approach to combining product, design, technology and data to develop solutions for customers.

India's Role In Capital One's Global Technology Network

Capital One India has served as an integral part of the company's global technology network since 2004. The centre brings together expertise across data science, AI, machine learning, software engineering and analytics to support the development and deployment of financial solutions for customers worldwide.

Capital One, a technology-led financial services company, uses proprietary data science, AI and modern software engineering across its primary markets. The Bengaluru centre supports this approach through its technology and engineering capabilities.

Vasudevan's appointment places him at the helm of the India organisation as the company continues to strengthen its technology capabilities and collaboration with global teams.

data.title: NDTV Appoints Ravi Srivastava As Chief Legal And Regulatory Officer
data.description:
The legal veteran brings over two decades of experience across broadcasting, media, telecom and regulated industries, including nearly nine years at Star India

NDTV has appointed Ravi Srivastava as Chief Legal and Regulatory Officer, strengthening its legal, regulatory and compliance leadership as the network continues to expand across television, digital and emerging platforms.Srivastava brings more than 20 years of experience leading legal, regulatory and governance functions across broadcasting, media, telecommunications and other regulated industries. His areas of expertise include regulatory compliance, commercial contracting, corporate governance, litigation and board-level advisory. Over the course of his career, he has built and led legal functions at several Indian and global organisations.

Prior to joining NDTV, Srivastava served as Group General Counsel at Ampersand Group, a diversified education and services organisation, where he led the group's legal function. Before that, he headed legal and regulatory functions at Intech Organics, served as Senior Vice President – Legal & Regulatory at Hathway Digital and was Head of Legal at Saregama India.

Nine Years At Star India

A significant part of Srivastava's career was spent at Star India, now part of 21st Century Fox's former portfolio, where he served as Vice President – Legal and Regulatory for nearly nine years.During his tenure, he was the designated compliance officer for Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) interconnect regulations. He also concluded a distribution agreement worth Rs 300 crore with a leading direct-to-home (DTH) operator.

Srivastava was involved in the establishment of the Broadcasting Content Complaints Council (BCCC) and contributed to amendments to the Cable Television Act that mandated digitisation. He also oversaw commercial contracts associated with the launch of Hotstar. His contributions were recognised with Star India's ‘Game Changers’ award for two consecutive years.He holds a Bachelor of Laws degree from the University of Delhi and a postgraduate degree from the Delhi School of Economics.

Legal Leadership At NDTV

Commenting on the appointment, Rahul Kanwal, CEO and Editor-in-Chief, NDTV, said that a strong legal and regulatory foundation would be essential as the network expands across television, digital and new platforms. He highlighted Srivastava's experience in broadcasting regulation and governance, adding that his track record in complex regulatory environments would support the organisation's growth.

Srivastava said the legal function must act as a strategic partner to the business in an evolving media and regulatory environment. He added that his focus would be on protecting the institution while enabling growth, and strengthening NDTV's governance and legal frameworks.In his new role, Srivastava will lead NDTV's legal, regulatory and compliance functions. His responsibilities will include advising the leadership team on governance, commercial partnerships, content and distribution matters, and regulatory affairs.

The appointment comes as NDTV continues to develop its portfolio of platforms, brands and partnerships, with a focus on strengthening its institutional and governance frameworks.

data.title: Greaves Cotton Targets Europe For Global Marine Business Expansion Through Multiflex
data.description:
The company is leveraging its engineering capabilities and international distribution network to expand its marine solutions business, with a presence in over 65 countries

Greaves Cotton Limited is accelerating its global marine business expansion through its Multiflex Marine brand, identifying Europe as a key growth market. The company is focusing on strengthening original equipment manufacturer (OEM) partnerships, expanding its distributor network and taking its India-developed engineering solutions to international markets.

The expansion strategy was showcased at METSTRADE 2026, held in Amsterdam, Netherlands, from November 17 to 19. Through its subsidiary Excel Controlinkage Private Limited, Greaves Cotton is strengthening Multiflex Marine as an integrated brand within its diversified engineering portfolio.

Multiflex Marine currently operates in more than 65 countries, serving over 400 customers through approximately 200 distributors.

Expands Marine Product Portfolio

As part of its international growth strategy, Multiflex Marine is expanding its marine control solutions portfolio to cater to recreational boats, commercial vessels, workboats, personal watercraft and boat trailers.

At METSTRADE 2026, the company launched its Multiflex Hydraulic Steering System for outboard applications ranging from 90HP to 500HP under the campaign theme 'Master Every Turn'. It also soft-launched Multiflex Electric Trim Tabs under the theme 'Level Up Your Ride'.

The showcase additionally featured EDGE Premium Engine Control Cables, designed to deliver enhanced control and performance. The company used the platform to strengthen engagement with international OEMs, distributors and other industry stakeholders.

Global Expansion Under GREAVES.NEXT Strategy

The expansion is aligned with Greaves Cotton's GREAVES.NEXT strategy, which focuses on evolving into a diversified engineering solutions provider and building businesses with global growth potential.

The company said it would continue to focus on customer requirements, product development and international partnerships to strengthen Multiflex Marine's position in the global marine solutions market.

data.title: Canada Hands Ford $300 Million After Finishing Plant Retooling
data.description:
By Paul Vieira

OTTAWA--Canada on Friday unveiled over $300 million in financing to Ford Motor after the automaker began production of its F-Series Super Duty pickup truck at a Toronto-area factory that underwent retooling prior to President Trump's hefty automobile tariffs.

Canadian Industry Minister Melanie Joly said the money underscores the government's efforts to maintain an auto sector in the country in the face of hefty tariffs from President Trump. The plant in Oakville, Ontario, was closed starting in 2024 for retooling to allow for the manufacturing of conventional and electrified versions of the Super Duty truck.

Ford's decision to follow through with production is in contrast to Stellantis, which is now engaged in a row with Joly and other Canadian officials. Stellantis received federal funding for a retooling of two of its Canadian factories. Stellantis then pivoted and shifted planned production of the Jeep Compass in Brampton, Ontario, to Illinois amid Trump's trade policy. Stellantis has struck a deal to sell the factory in Brampton, Ontario, to a local defense firm.

Ford's Oakville decision "was an act of resistance. Canadians know a lot about resistence these days," said Joly, in reference to the automaker's push to build pickup trucks in Canada amid a trade row with Washington.

"Our strategy is based on our clear conviction that Canada is an auto nation and intends to continue to do so," Joly said at a formal reopening of the Oakville plant. "We will continue to invest in automakers that invest in us."

Stellantis has offered to repay some of the money Canada provided for past support. Stellantis Chief Executive Antonio Filosa is set to speak with Joly later Friday, and the Canadian minister reiterated her threat to launch a lawsuit against the automaker unless it reconsiders its plans for Brampton. "If they go ahead and sell the plant, well, then they will face legal recourses from the government of Canada of hundreds of millions of dollars," she told reporters in Oakville.

She added Canada is open to provide Stellantis with additional financial support should it choose to maintain operations in Brampton.

Write to Paul Vieira at paul.vieira@wsj.com

data.title: Michael Burry Locks In Gains on Nvidia, Chipmaker ETF Puts As AI Rout Deepens
data.description:
Key points:
  • The ‘Big Short’ investor sold half of his Nvidia and VanEck Semiconductor ETF puts at a profit. 
  • The trades come as Nvidia is set to drop for the seventh consecutive trading session.
  • Burry bought an additional 20% in MercadoLibre (MELI) and highlighted “absolute relative strength” in a few healthcare stocks.

The ‘Big Short’ famed investor Michael Burry locked in profits on half of his bearish bets against Nvidia Corp. (NVDA) and an ETF that tracks the semiconductor sector on Friday, capitalizing on a steep technology sell-off this week while maintaining a long-term bearish bet on the Nasdaq 100.

In a Friday update to subscribers of his ‘Cassandra Unchained’ Substack, Burry said he sold 50% of his put options on both Nvidia and the VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH), locking in what he described as substantial gains while keeping the remaining half open. Put options gain value when the underlying shares decline.

Burry also pared back bullish exposure elsewhere, selling roughly one-third of his call options on animal health company Zoetis Inc. (ZTS) to secure profits. At the same time, he left his bearish April 2027 put options on the Nasdaq 100 completely untouched, signaling continued caution toward large-cap technology valuations.

Meanwhile, Burry boosted his stake in Latin American e-commerce giant MercadoLibre Inc. (MELI) by 20% and highlighted “absolute relative strength” in a few healthcare stocks like Molina Healthcare (MOH) and HCA Healthcare (HCA), as well as Photoshop maker Adobe (ADBE) and Sprouts Farmers Market (SFM).

NVDA Stock Set For Worst Week Since 2018

Burry’s profit-taking coincided with a punishing week for Nvidia shares, which extended a seven-session losing streak on Friday. The chipmaker’s stock was also on track to record its worst weekly performance since November 2018. The stock has been in constant turmoil ever since former CEO Jensen Huang accepted his romantic involvement with alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang.

A strong quarterly earnings print and a rosy outlook did little to prop up the share price of the chipmaker, which currently sits at the very top of the entire AI infrastructure buildout. Earlier this week, Nvidia reported that revenue more than doubled year-over-year to a record $115.8 billion, while net profit surged 109% to $64.9 billion, topping Wall Street forecasts. Interim CEO Colette Kress also guided fourth-quarter revenue to $130 billion and raised the company's fiscal 2028 revenue growth outlook to 75%.

Meanwhile, two House Democrats reportedly opened an inquiry into whether Nvidia sought to influence the Commerce Department’s investigation of Megaspeed, a Singapore-based cloud company suspected of illegally diverting advanced chips to China.

Furthermore, Congressional summonses to Nvidia executives have also dampened sentiment. Representative Brett Guthrie, chairman of the House Committee on Energy and Commerce, sent a letter to Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress earlier this week requesting company officials appear before the panel no later than December. 2.

Chipmakers And Tech Stocks Tumble 

Nvidia's slump rippled across wider technology and semiconductor stocks throughout the week, dragging major indexes sharply lower as investors questioned whether massive corporate spending on artificial intelligence infrastructure will deliver adequate returns.

The tech-heavy Invesco QQQ ETF (QQQ), which tracks the Nasdaq 100, was down nearly 9% on the week. Rival U.S. chipmakers suffered even steeper Friday drops, with Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) plunging more than 11% and memory chipmaker Micron Technology (MU) sliding over 13% amid broader valuation and supply chain concerns.

NVDA, SMH Stock: Retail View 

Retail sentiment around Nvidia on Stocktwits remained in the ‘extremely bullish’ zone with ‘extremely high’ message volumes and was in ‘bearish’ territory towards the VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH).

NVDA stock has lost about 28% year-to-date, while the SMH added around 13% during the same period.

data.title: Bitcoin Drops Below $59K, Wiping Out $1.5B In Crypto Bets: MSTR, BMNR, ASST Stocks Extend Losses
data.description:
Key points:
  • Bitcoin has fallen around 33% this year and remains over 50% below its record high of over $126,000 seen in October last year. 
  • The apex cryptocurrency has erased its entire August-September recovery to around $83,000, and was trading about 3% above its recent bear-market low.
  • CoinGlass data showed $1.53 billion in cryptocurrency bets had been forced to unwind in the last 24 hours, with long positions accounting for $1.4 billion of the wipeout. 

Bitcoin (BTC) dropped below $59,000 in afternoon trade on Friday for the first time since July, wiping out over $1.5 billion in cryptocurrency bets, as tech stocks continued to pull down broader markets.

Bitcoin’s price fell nearly 6% in the last 24 hours to $58,900. It was among the top trending tickers on Stocktwits at the time of writing. The apex cryptocurrency was on track for a seventh consecutive weekly decline, its longest since the drawdown of April 2022.

The sell-off was accompanied by heavy withdrawals from U.S. spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds, including a record daily outflow from BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT).

CoinGlass data showed $1.53 billion in cryptocurrency bets had been forced to unwind in the last 24 hours, with long positions accounting for $1.4 billion of the wipeout. A third of the liquidations were in Bitcoin alone, amounting to around $540 million.

Altcoins Take A Bigger Hit Than Bitcoin

Leading altcoins took a bigger hit than Bitcoin in the crypto sell-off. Ethereum (ETH) fell over 8%, sliding to around $1,600, while Ripple’s XRP (XRP) fell almost 7%, remaining below the $1 mark. Retail sentiment around Ethereum trended in ‘bullish’ territory over the past day, while sentiment around XRP trended in the ‘bearish’ zone.

The weakness in digital assets coincided with another sharp decline in technology stocks. Anthropic (ANT) shares fell 11% to around $86 in midday trading, nearly erasing their gains from Thursday’s debut and leaving the stock only slightly above its $83 IPO price.

The iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) sank another 7.8%, while the Nasdaq dropped 3%, both reaching their weakest levels since April. Retail sentiment around SOXX on Stocktwits continued to trend in ‘bearish’ territory over the past day, while chatter rose to ‘normal’ from ‘low’ levels.

The Nasdaq-100 tracking Invesco QQQ Trust Series 1 (QQQ) was down 3.8% and also saw an uptick in chatter to ‘high’ from ‘normal’ levels. Sentiment around the ETF remained in ‘bullish’ territory over the past day.

Bitcoin-Linked Stocks Extend Their Declines

The cryptocurrency sell-off also weighed on crypto-linked stocks, adding to pressure from the broader market decline. Bitcoin treasury firms Strategy (MSTR) and Strive (ASST), as well as Ethereum treasury company BitMine Immersion Technologies (BMNR), all fell and were among the top trending tickers on Stocktwits at the time of writing.

MSTR shares fell around 6.6%, while ASST stock dropped nearly 10% and BMNR stock declined 8.5%. Retail sentiment around Strategy tipped to ‘extremely bearish’ from ‘bearish’ territory over the past day, accompanied by ‘high’ levels of chatter. Bitmine, on the other hand, saw retail sentiment improve to ‘neutral’ from the ‘bearish’ zone.

Meanwhile, cryptocurrency exchange Coinbase (COIN) and USDC stablecoin issuer (CRCL) each fell only 2% each.

The losses were steeper among Bitcoin miners that have spent the past year expanding into AI computing and data center infrastructure. Hut 8 (HUT) led the decline, plunging nearly 15%, followed by Core Scientific (CORZ) and Bitdeer Technologies (BTDR), which fell more than 13% each.

IREN (IREN), CleanSpark (CLSK), Cipher Mining (CIFR) and Keel Infrastructure (KEEL) dropped roughly 12% to 13%. MARA Holdings (MARA), HIVE Digital Technologies (HIVE) and TeraWulf (WULF) lost about 11%, while Riot Platforms (RIOT) held up relatively better, declining 8.5%.

How Is Retail Feeling About Bitcoin?

Retail sentiment on Stocktwits around Bitcoin remained in ‘bearish’ territory over the past day, even as chatter stayed at ‘extremely high’ levels.

Retail traders on the platform were perplexed by the drop and speculating about when the apex cryptocurrency will finally hit bottom.

View this Stocktwits post
View this Stocktwits post

Bitcoin has now erased its entire August-September rebound, which had taken the cryptocurrency to around $83,000. At approximately $58,900, it was just 3% above its recent bear-market low of around $57,000.

The apex cryptocurrency has fallen around 33% this year and remains over 50% below its record high of over $126,000 seen in October last year.

data.title: JPMorgan says Bitcoin price drop widens gap to $86,000 production cost
data.description:
Mining a Bitcoin costs about $86,000, according to JPMorgan. The market currently values it far lower.

The bank's estimate of Bitcoin's production cost now sits more than $26,000 above the market price. That gap could push higher-cost miners to sell more of the coins they've been holding in reserve.

JPMorgan analysts led by Nikolaos Panigirtzoglou published the report on Wednesday. Their central estimate puts Bitcoin's production cost at $86,000.

When the note came out, Bitcoin was trading near $65,000. That left a shortfall of about $21,000 between what the asset fetched and what it costs, on average, to produce.

Two days later, things got worse. On Friday, Bitcoin slipped below $60,000 for the first time since July, stretching the gap past $26,000.

For Bitcoin miners, the electricity bills and hardware costs don't pause when prices fall. The coins they mine are worth less, but the inputs cost the same.

JPMorgan didn't pin the decline on mining economics alone. The analysts pointed to several broader forces weighing on the market.

First, crypto exchange-traded funds saw significant outflows. According to the report, retail investors have been rotating out of crypto ETFs and into stock ETFs.

Second, technology stocks have been deteriorating. Bitcoin has often traded in sympathy with risk assets, so weakness in tech tends to spill over.

Third, expectations around Federal Reserve rate cuts have shifted. When the market prices in fewer or later cuts, speculative assets tend to lose some of their appeal.

JPMorgan suggested that many unprofitable miners may be forced to sell their Bitcoin reserves. Some would sell to cover operating costs. Others might sell to fund a pivot into other businesses, such as artificial intelligence.

JPMorgan's production cost figure has also moved around this year. Earlier estimates in 2026 ranged from $77,000 to $85,000 before landing at the current $86,000.

That upward drift means the bar for profitability has been rising even as the price has been falling. Miners are getting squeezed from both directions.

There's a reason analysts watch production cost so closely. Historically, it has tended to act as a soft floor for Bitcoin's price.

The logic runs like this. When price falls well below cost, the least efficient miners shut off their machines. Fewer machines means less total computing power securing the network, a measure called hashrate.

Bitcoin then adjusts its mining difficulty to match. When fewer miners compete, the puzzle gets easier, and the remaining miners earn coins more cheaply.

The JPMorgan analysts said the gap between price and production cost could narrow if higher-cost operations exit. In that scenario, hashrate and difficulty would adjust downward, lowering the average cost to mine.

Note the word "soft." A soft floor is not a guarantee. Price can trade below production cost for extended periods, and it often does during bear phases.

For traders, the immediate concern is supply. If struggling miners dump reserves to stay afloat or fund AI pivots, that selling lands on a market already dealing with ETF outflows and nervous macro conditions.

For mining companies, the divide between efficient and inefficient operators is about to get sharper. Firms with cheap power and newer hardware can ride out a stretch below the average cost. Those near the top of the cost curve face harder choices: sell coins, cut operations, or change business models entirely.

The macro backdrop still matters, too. JPMorgan tied part of the selloff to tech weakness, ETF rotation, and shifting Fed expectations.

For now, the gap stands at more than $26,000 and the miners are the ones holding the bill.

data.title: TIDEWATER MIDSTREAM AND INFRASTRUCTURE LTD. ANNOUNCES THE FILING OF THE MANAGEMENT INFORMATION CIRCULAR FOR ITS SPECIAL MEETING OF SHAREHOLDERS, IN CONNECTION WITH THE PROPOSED PLAN OF ARRANGEMENT WITH TIDEWATER RENEWABLES LTD.
data.description:
(TSX: TWM)

CALGARY, AB, Nov. 20, 2026 /CNW/ -- Tidewater Midstream and Infrastructure Ltd. () ("TWM", "Midstream" or the "Company") is pleased to announce that it has filed its notice of meeting, management information circular (the "Circular") and related documents (collectively, the "Meeting Materials") with applicable securities regulators in connection with a special meeting of TWM shareholders (the "TWM Shareholders"), to be held on Monday, December 14, 2026 (the "Meeting"). At the Meeting, TWM Shareholders will be asked to consider an ordinary resolution (the "Share Issuance Resolution") to approve the issuance of TWM common shares ("TWM Shares") issuable pursuant to a proposed arrangement (the "Arrangement") under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta), pursuant to which TWM will acquire all of the common shares ("TWR Shares") of Tidewater Renewables Ltd. ("TWR" or "Renewables") not already owned by TWM.

  • The Directors of Tidewater Midstream and Infrastructure Ltd. eligible to vote unanimously recommend that the Company's shareholders vote FOR the Share Issuance Resolution
  • Your vote is important no matter how many shares you own. Vote today!

The Arrangement

Under the terms of the arrangement agreement between TWM and TWR dated November 1, 2026 (the "Arrangement Agreement"), holders of TWR Shares (other than TWM) will receive 0.88 of a TWM Share for each TWR Share (the "Consideration").

Unanimous Board Recommendation and Reasons for the Board's Recommendation

The Arrangement is the result of an extensive and thorough arm's-length negotiation process between the special committee of independent directors (the "TWM Special Committee") of the board of directors of TWM (the "TWM Board") and the special committee of independent directors of the board of directors of TWR and their respective advisors.

The TWM Board, having undertaken a thorough review of, and having carefully considered, among other things, the unanimous recommendation of the TWM Special Committee, information concerning TWR, TWM, the Arrangement and its impact on TWM and affected stakeholders, unanimously recommends (with two directors, one of whom is an officer and both of whom are directors of TWR, abstaining and recusing themselves prior to the vote of the independent directors) that TWM Shareholders vote FOR the Share Issuance Resolution at the Meeting.

In making their determinations and recommendations that TWM Shareholders vote FOR the Share Issuance Resolution, the TWM Special Committee and the TWM Board considered and relied upon a number of factors, including the following:

  • Simplified Corporate Structure: The Arrangement will combine two closely integrated public companies under a unified governance structure to better execute on the combined company's growth strategy
  • Capital Markets Positioning: The increased scale and larger combined market capitalization are expected to improve access to capital markets, with combined company shareholders benefitting from increased public float and trading liquidity. Together with a simplified structure and streamlined messaging, the combined company is expected to be better positioned to attract institutional investors and to have enhanced alternatives for any future financing requirements.
  • Improved Financial Strength and Financing Flexibility: An improved credit profile and capital allocation are expected to build on the optimization potential of each company's existing balance sheet and create additional flexibility to finance future growth opportunities. TWM has received fully underwritten commitments from National Bank of Canada and ATB Financial for secured credit facilities to enhance the financing flexibility of the combined company, refinance existing debt and for general corporate purposes, subject to completion of the Arrangement, which are expected to provide the combined company with enhanced liquidity and refreshed committed tenor.
  • Scale and Diversification: The combined company will have an enhanced strategic position and a more diversified asset base, better positioning it for value-enhancing commercial opportunities across midstream, conventional and renewable fuels.
  • Value Creation Opportunities: The combined company is expected to benefit from operating efficiencies and corporate synergies through public company cost savings, reduced administrative burden and potential tax synergies.

Based on the TWR Shares outstanding as of November 5, 2026, TWM expects to issue approximately 12.8 million TWM Shares to TWR shareholders (other than TWM) under the Arrangement, representing approximately 37% of the outstanding TWM Shares immediately following the Arrangement. Including TWM Shares issuable on the exercise or settlement of TWR equity-based awards and for rounding, the Share Issuance Resolution will authorize the issuance of up to 13,843,838 TWM Shares.

The foregoing is a summary only and is qualified by the more detailed description of the reasons for the recommendation, and of the risks and other factors considered by the TWM Special Committee and the TWM Board, contained in the Circular.

We encourage TWM Shareholders to read the Circular for more detailed information. The Circular is available under TWM's profile on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.ca and on TWM's website at www.tidewatermidstream.com.

Required Approvals

In order to become effective, the Share Issuance Resolution must be approved by: (a) a simple majority of the votes cast by TWM Shareholders present in person or represented by proxy at the Meeting, including on a disinterested basis, excluding the votes cast by TWM insiders who will receive TWM Shares under the Arrangement, as required by the TSX; and (b) a simple majority of the votes cast by TWM Shareholders present in person or represented by proxy at the Meeting, excluding the votes attached to TWM Shares held by any "interested party", any "related party" of an "interested party" or any "joint actor" of the foregoing as required under Multilateral Instrument 61-101 – Protection of Minority Security Holders in Special Transactions. Completion of the Arrangement is also subject to, among other things, approval by TWR shareholders of the Arrangement, the approval of the Court of King's Bench of Alberta, and other customary closing conditions. Subject to the satisfaction or waiver of such conditions, the Arrangement is expected to be completed on or about December 18, 2026.

Voting and Support Agreements

Directors and executive officers of TWM holding TWM Shares and other key TWM Shareholders, collectively holding approximately 41% of the outstanding TWM Shares have entered into support agreements with TWR (the "TWM Support Agreements"). Pursuant to the TWM Support Agreements, each holder agreed, among other things, to vote or cause to be voted all TWM Shares of which such holder is the registered and/or beneficial owner, or over which it exercises control or direction (including, subject to limited exceptions, any such securities acquired after the date of the applicable TWM Support Agreement), in favour of the Share Issuance Resolution and any other matter that could reasonably be expected to facilitate the Arrangement, and against any matter that could reasonably be expected to delay, prevent or frustrate the successful completion of the Arrangement.

Vote Today

The proxy voting deadline is 9:00 a.m. (Calgary time) on Thursday, December 10, 2026. TWM Shareholders are encouraged to vote well in advance of the proxy voting deadline to ensure their vote is submitted in a timely manner. TWM Shareholders may vote online, by telephone or by any other methods provided in the form of proxy or voting instruction form included in the Meeting Materials.

About Tidewater Midstream and Infrastructure Ltd.

Tidewater Midstream and Infrastructure Ltd. is traded on the TSX under the symbol "TWM". Midstream's business objective is to build a diversified midstream and infrastructure company across the North American gas processing, natural gas liquids ("NGL"), petroleum refining, and renewables markets. Midstream's strategy is to profitably grow and create shareholder value by acquiring and building high quality, strategically located infrastructure. To achieve its business objective, Midstream is focused on providing customers with a full service, vertically integrated value chain through the acquisition and development of energy infrastructure, including downstream facilities, natural gas processing facilities, NGL infrastructure, pipelines, storage, and various renewable initiatives. To complement its infrastructure asset base, Midstream also markets crude oil, refined products, natural gas, NGLs and renewable products and services to customers across North America.

Midstream's downstream assets supply refined products to a niche market and provide an asset base for renewables initiatives. The key downstream assets include the PGR, the sole light oil refinery within the interior British Columbia market, and the Renewable Diesel and Renewable Hydrogen Complex (the "HDRD Complex") owned by Renewables. The PGR refines crude oil feedstock into gasoline and diesel and is where Midstream's co-processing activities take place. The HDRD Complex is also located in Prince George, adjacent to the PGR.

Midstream's key midstream assets include: the Brazeau River Complex, a full-service natural gas and NGL processing facility with natural gas storage pools, and the Ram River Gas Plant, a sour natural gas processing facility with sulfur handling solutions and rail connections.

Additional information relating to Midstream is available on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.ca and at www.tidewatermidstream.com.

About Tidewater Renewables Ltd.

Tidewater Renewables Ltd. is an energy transition company. Renewables is focused on the production of low carbon fuels, primarily renewable diesel. Renewables was created in response to the growing demand for renewable fuels in North America and to capitalize on its potential to efficiently turn a wide variety of renewable feedstocks (such as canola oil, tallow, used cooking oil, distillers corn oil, soybean oil, and other biomasses) into low carbon fuels. Renewables' objective is to become a leading Canadian renewable fuel producer. Renewables is pursuing this objective through the ownership, development, and operation of clean fuels projects and related infrastructure that utilize existing proven technologies.

Additional information relating to Renewables is available on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.ca and at www.tidewater-renewables.com.

data.title: US energy firms add rigs; count highest since April 2024 - Baker Hughes
data.description:
US energy firms this week added rigs for a second time in five weeks, energy services firm Baker Hughes said in its closely followed report on Friday.

The total oil and gas rig count, an early indicator of future output, rose by six to 607 in the week to November 20, its highest since April 26, 2024. (BHGUSWTT), (BHGUSOILDRLW), (BHGUSGASDRLW) (USOIRC=ECI), (USGSRC=ECI)

Baker Hughes said this week's increase puts the total rig count up 53 rigs, or 9.6% above this time last year.

Baker Hughes said oil rigs rose by six to 469 this week, their highest since May 2025, while gas rigs rose by one to 128, and other miscellaneous rigs fell by one to 10.

The oil and gas rig count declined by 7% in 2025, 5% in 2024, and 20% in 2023 as lower US oil prices prompted energy firms to focus more on boosting shareholder returns and paying down debt rather than increasing output.

But now with spot US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude prices expected to rise in 2026 for the first time in four years due to supply disruptions from the Iran war, the US Energy Information Administration (EIA) projected that crude output will rise from a record 13.7 million barrels per day (bpd) in 2025 to 13.9 million bpd in 2026, while seeing gas output jumping from a record 107.6 billion cubic feet per day (bcfd) in 2025 to 113.0 bcfd in 2026.

The Middle East conflict has caused the biggest disruption ever to global oil and gas trade and could cut world oil demand by more than 4% by 2035 if governments accelerate electrification, efficiency and fuel-switching measures in response, the International Energy Agency (IEA) said on Thursday.

data.title: Binance hack laundering ramps up as $149 million in bitcoin mixed through coinjoins: Elliptic
data.description:
Launderers allegedly linked to North Korea are now mixing tens of millions of dollars in bitcoin a day in a bid to make tracing the funds harder.

At least 2,310 BTC, worth around $149 million at the time, has been mixed through coinjoin transactions, with roughly 90% of that occurring since Tuesday, Elliptic said in a Friday update.

Coinjoins are a method of obfuscating the source of a bitcoin transaction by combining different users' transactions. This makes it harder to match senders' and recipients' coins.

This follows transfers of around 488,000 ETH, valued at $860 million, from five wallets. Most of this ether is now parked in new addresses, minus around $70 million that was swapped to bitcoin through THORChain. That BTC was subsequently mixed within hours.

The report's author, Tom Robinson, noted the coinjoins were organized by Kruw, a Wasabi Wallet coordinator. Coordinators arrange the transactions to be mixed but don't take custody of users' funds.

The 18,720 BTC stolen directly from Binance are still untouched. The bitcoins being mixed stem from swaps of other stolen assets like ETH, XRP and SOL.

Difficult to cash out

Despite this, Elliptic said very little has likely been cashed out. The firm's latest tally puts about $2.35 billion in wallets linked to the theft, while $2.85 billion is frozen.

Separately, Binance said Wednesday that it obtained a $6.5 billion worldwide freeze order from the Abu Dhabi Global Market Courts against the attackers. Additional court orders give issuers and exchanges the green light to return stolen assets that they've already frozen.

Binance previously described the October breach as a monthslong campaign involving malicious software, a fake job interview and compromised internal AI tooling that gave attackers access to the exchange's wallet-signing systems.
